tasks.task: Write weekly notices and a read-aloud version

items.when: Each week on news day, to gather items, chase missing facts and run the sign-off in order
When you need the notice sheet, a short newsletter and a version to read out loud
When the same edition runs every week and should be drafted and checked against past issues
When the notices go by email, to compare subject lines from several angles
When the read-aloud version is drafted, to fix lines that trip when spoken
Before sending, to swap stiff words for plain ones and see each cut explained

tasks.task: Write a monthly or term newsletter

items.when: When the newsletter has no fixed shape, to set its sections, readers and rhythm
When you have the news and dates and need the edition in the organisation's voice
Before sending, to pick a subject line from several honest options
When an item rambles, to find its point and cut what the reader does not need
When the edition is drafted, to get cuts, subject fixes and a score before it goes

tasks.task: Send an urgent notice about a closure or change

items.when: When people must know now: a closure, a change of time or place, or a safety message
When the problem will run on, to plan the first notice, the updates and the all-clear
Before the next emergency, to set fallback channels, owners and when to switch
When some families read another language, to send the same notice in each one
When the notice hides the news in soft words, to say what happened and what to do
Before it goes out, to make sure the action and the time are plain in the first lines

tasks.task: Write a welcome and follow-up set for newcomers

items.when: Before writing, to plan what each message does so one builds on the last
When a new family, member or visitor should get a warm welcome and one clear next step
When the first message must be opened, to compare several subject lines
Before writing the set, to plan three different orders for the messages and draft each first one
When the set is drafted, to check length, pace and the one ask in each message
When the three welcome plans are drafted, so someone who did not write them picks one

tasks.task: Turn staff notes into parent updates and progress notes

items.when: When staff notes are thin, to set a simple way to record learning and share it with families
At the end of a week or term, to turn notes on several children into kind, honest updates
When a note labels a child, to describe what happened and what helps instead
When a note carries a concern, to compare a warmer and a firmer wording of the same facts
Before sending, to cut teacher jargon a parent would not know

tasks.task: Write an announcement to all staff, parents or members

items.when: When one message goes to everyone and must say what, why, when and who to ask
When staff hear first, to add talking points for leaders, a question list and a rollout order
When the news will raise hard questions, to write them down with straight answers
When the announcement goes by email, to choose a subject line that says the news
When staff, parents and the public each get a version, to find where they contradict

tasks.task: Write a hard message gently

items.when: When you need a policy reminder or a hard update written kindly and clearly
When there is a setback to report: what was lost, the numbers and what happens next
When the organisation got something wrong and must own it and say what changes
When you are unsure of the tone, to see the same facts in two or three tones
When the draft is kind but unclear, or clear but cold
When replying to an upset parent or member, to check promises, facts and tone

tasks.task: Rewrite a policy, letter or form in plain language

items.when: When a policy, letter or notice is stiff or full of jargon and must keep its meaning
When a new policy must be explained to staff with what changed and what to do
When the piece is a form or a set of steps, to use the words readers already say
When long words and passive sentences hide who must do what
When the rewrite is done, to check nothing was lost and each cut has a reason

tasks.task: Write a house style guide from past messages

items.when: When you have past newsletters and letters, to pull out the voice with examples
When you need voice, tone shifts, words to use and avoid, and how names and dates are written
When tone must change by situation: welcome, reminder, bad news, celebration
When volunteers need one page with word lists and before and after lines
When the guide is agreed, to check each new draft against it before it goes out

tasks.task: Build the comms calendar and sign-off chain for a term or season

items.when: Before a term, church season or campaign starts, to plan it once from the key dates
When you need one calendar across every channel with an owner and approver per message
When one event or push needs its own brief with messages, channels and a week-by-week plan
When email is the main channel and you need a month of sends planned
When social posts should follow the same calendar on a rolling basis

tasks.task: Write an invitation pack for a festival or special event

items.when: When the aim is to fill seats, to plan who to invite, through which channels and the follow-up
When guests have access needs, to plan what the invitation must tell them
When you need the invitation, the notice and the reminder in the organisation's voice
When the invitation needs a headline, to compare five angles for people who have never come
When the pack includes a poster, for a guided run to checked text and a layout
Before it goes out, to check the invitation works for screen readers and large print

tasks.task: Check a newsletter, document or poster for accessibility

items.when: When an email, Word file, PDF or poster must be readable by everyone
When the organisation's colours are used behind text, to check each pair is readable
When the piece is a slide deck for an assembly or meeting
When the newsletter also lives on the website and the page itself needs checking

tasks.task: Structure and write an annual or impact report

items.when: Before writing, to plan the report and check facts, numbers and names
When the numbers are thin, to decide what to measure and who tracks it for next year
When you have data and case notes and need honest numbers beside real stories
When a table of numbers needs a point, the proof and a next step
To try opening the report on one real case and not a summary
When a big number sounds good, to ask what it counts and what to compare it with
Before print, to check every figure and claim against its source

tasks.task: Write impact stories from case notes

items.when: When you have one interview, to outline the story and list what evidence is missing
When you need a person's own words, to ask with three easy questions
When the story is about a real person, to write it with consent and checked facts
When you have many cases, to pick the one to build on and its surprise
When the story is drafted, to cut sector words the person would never say

tasks.task: Plan numbers pages with chart specs

items.when: When you must choose which few numbers earn a page
When each number needs the right chart and a check that it does not mislead
When a page of figures could work as one infographic, to try a layout and style
When a chart is crowded, to strip it to the one thing the reader should see
When charts are placed, to write alt text and long descriptions and check contrast

tasks.task: Write a two-page summary for funders

items.when: When the full report exists and you must pick what a funder needs first
When a long report must become a short summary with the answer first
When the summary runs past two pages, to keep the main idea and cut what fights it

tasks.task: Plan a page-by-page layout for a report

items.when: When the report carries a lot of text and needs a grid, a short type list and white space
Before settling the layout, to see three alternatives to the template look
When pages are drafted, to check type size, spacing and line length

tasks.task: Write a 'what to expect' or enrolment page

items.when: When you have the real questions newcomers ask and the answers
When the page needs a headline, sections and one clear next step
When the top of the page is flat, to compare five headlines with a subhead and button
When the page is drafted, to walk it as a first-time visitor and see where they stall

tasks.task: Write enquiry replies and answers that cut repeat questions

items.when: When the same questions keep coming, to list them from posts and messages
When an enquiry needs a reply in the right tone with the next step
When repeat questions should be answered once, on a page or in a welcome pack
When a reply sounds curt, to see it warmer with the same facts
Before saving a reply as a template, to make sure a new parent would follow it

tasks.task: Write social posts for the community

items.when: When posts are ad hoc, to set a rolling calendar tied to the organisation's dates
When one piece of news needs a post made for each platform
Before posting, to check each post still sounds like the organisation

tasks.task: Write a notice for local press

items.when: When there is news for the local paper or radio: who to send it to and the pitch
Before sending, to list the hard questions a reporter may ask and the answers

tasks.task: Write a volunteer or giving appeal

items.when: When asking for volunteers, to define the roles and what is asked of each
When asking members or donors to give: the copy, the amounts and the schedule
When the appeal goes by email, to compare subject lines that are honest about the ask
When the appeal is drafted, to check length, pace and one clear ask

always.when: When a draft is done, to check it against the organisation's voice and fix what drifts
When a message gives dates, names, numbers or rules, to check each against its source
Before delivery, to catch stock phrases that make a message read as machine written
Last step before sign-off, to catch slips with a log of every change
Before a message goes out, so a fresh reader checks it against the brief as a parent or member would

helpers.when: When a poster, invitation or sign needs a real layout and print-ready files
When the annual report needs a designed page layout or a deck version
When the numbers pages need charts built, not only chosen and described
When the report or appeal feeds a grant bid or a donor campaign
When notices must go out in several languages for families and members
When a tutor or school needs a lesson or scheme-of-work outline, not a message about one

gaps: No library item writes for schools, nurseries or faith groups; parent notes, daily updates and report comments rest on the kit alone
No library item writes an urgent notice in versions for text, email, door sign and phone tree; the outage pack is for services
No library item measures the reading age of a draft
No library item checks Word files, PDFs or email newsletters for accessibility; the checkers are for web pages and slides
No library item writes an invitation pack, an order of service or content for a faith season
No library item writes a first-visit or enrolment page; general page and FAQ writers stand in
No library item sets a sign-off chain for messages, with who approves what and a fallback approver
No library item checks a newsletter for children's names and photos used without consent
No library item makes clearly different options for a funder summary, social posts or a press notice for a community group
No library item writes a welcome pack for new families or members; the welcome flows are built for shops
